title: run-epic/settle now exec `gh auth token` at startup even for repos that declare no close-out rule
description:
pullRequestsForRun resolves its credential unconditionally at run start, so after vo4 a machine with gh installed and no GITHUB_TOKEN runs one `gh auth token` subprocess per `ticfac run-epic`/`ticfac settle` even when the target repo declares no PR + CI rule (the result is then discarded with the nil surface). The behavior is correct — it is the price of the ladder — but tick 9sz already plans 'when, and only when, the close-out rule needs a forge': its implementation can read the rule first (reconcile.ReadCloseoutRule) and skip the resolution entirely, or pullRequestsForRun can accept a rule argument.

ticfac run epic-2jn created this tick by absorbing the finding b7dae6a368c133ce9a7d2c9bfffbbb77abdd423ec35d3b1e2e40cc6ad15e8dec (reported by run-epic-2jn/tick-vo4/attempt-7): the finding was judged against the epic's definition of done and gates the done, naming no single item (the fallback names every item at risk in its reason). The decision record — item id, verdict, observed or predicted, confidence — is .ticfac/runs/epic-2jn/absorptions/b7dae6a368c133ce9a7d2c9bfffbbb77abdd423ec35d3b1e2e40cc6ad15e8dec.json on the run branch.
